how does en passant work

En passant is a special pawn capture. If a pawn advances two squares from its starting rank and lands directly beside an enemy pawn, that enemy pawn can capture it as if it had moved only one square, but only on the very next move. For example, if White plays e2-e4 with a Black pawn on d4, Black can play dxe3, removing the e4 pawn. If Black doesn't capture right away, the option is gone.

The classic corner mate is the back-rank-style smothered mate, where a knight mates a king boxed in by its own pieces. The standard example has the Black king on h8, a Black rook on g8 and a pawn on h7 (or g7), and White's knight lands on f7 for mate: Nf7#. The most famous version is the Philidor's Legacy finish, 1...Qg1+ 2.Rxg1 Nf2+ 3.Kg1... in short, Qg8+ Rxg8 Nf7#. The point is that the king's own pieces take away every escape square, so a single knight check is enough.

A pawn reaching the last rank must promote to a queen, rook, bishop, or knight of its own color. It can't stay a pawn and can't become a king.
